points.text: M1: molecule with a non super-(im)posable mirror image
M2: [structural formula diagram of 1,5-dichloro-2,4-dimethylpentane: Cl-C(CH3)2-CH2-CH(CH3)-CH2-Cl with chiral centre at C4 indicated]
[structural formula diagram of 1,3-dichloro-1,1,3-trimethyl? i.e. (CH3)2C(Cl)-CH2-C(Cl)(CH3)2 with Cl atoms below the chain]

M1: Method 1: show number of mol gas produced from 0.241 g $\text{NCl}_3$ [$M_r(\text{NCl}_3)=120.5$; 1 mol $\text{NCl}_3$ produces 2 mol gas] $n = 2 \times 0.241 / 120.5$ OR $n = 0.0040$ mol gas produced. OR Method 2: calculate mol produced from 0.241 g $\text{NCl}_3$: 0.003 mol $\text{Cl}_2$ AND 0.001 mol $\text{N}_2$
M2: correct conversion of T to Kelvin, V to $\text{m}^3$ and correct value of R in all $PV/RT$ equations used

M3: Method 1: use $P = nRT/V$ with M2 values for $n$, $R$, $T$ and $V$ to find pressure of gas produced; increase in $p = nRT/V = (0.0040 \times 8.31 \times 293)/(250 \times 10^{-6}) = 3.90 \times 10^{4}$. OR Method 2: use $PV/RT = n$ for both calculations or combined equation with M2 values for $R$, $T$ and $V$ to find partial pressure for each gas; $pp\text{Cl}_2 = 29217.96$ AND $pp\text{N}_2 = 9739.32$

M4: Method 1: $= 1.00 \times 10^{5} + M3$ (Pa); total pressure $= 1.00 \times 10^{5} + 3.90 \times 10^{4} = 1.39 \times 10^{5}$ (Pa). OR Method 2: Use $P_{total} = pp$ unreacted gas $+ pp\text{Cl}_2 + pp\text{N}_2$; $1 \times 10^{5} + 2.92 \times 10^{4} + 9.74 \times 10^{3} = 138940$
